title: Alibaba Bets $10B on AI Video While Chip Smugglers Face Charges
tldr: Alibaba is raising $10.2B for AI investment and widening access to Wan 3.0, a video model that generates 30-second clips from almost any input.
Taiwan indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager and two Super Micro employees, over an alleged scheme to smuggle US-controlled AI servers into China.
Sam Altman blames slow agentic AI adoption on 'economic inertia' -- companies that are scaling agents successfully share three specific practices worth copying.

tips.heading: Build and launch a website with ChatGPT Sites
steps: Open the ChatGPT desktop app and switch to the Codex tab.
Click Sites in the left panel, then Create new site -- describe what you want built or upload a reference file for context.
Preview the site privately, tell ChatGPT what to change, then click Publish for a shareable URL.
Return to the same project any time you need an update -- describe the change, preview it, publish again.
tips.prompt:
@Sites Create a website to build an interactive project tracker for my marketing team. Include task owners, deadlines, priorities, progress, and filters for status.

Add a dashboard showing completed, overdue, and upcoming tasks. Make the design cleaner and more professional.

news.body: Alibaba is raising $10.2B for AI investment and widened access to its new video model. The stock fell on the fundraise news; Wan 3.0 can generate clips up to 30 seconds long from nearly any input -- text, video, documents, spreadsheets, slides, or webpages.
news.means: Worth a quick eval alongside Sora/Veo for any client considering AI video for marketing or training content -- the input flexibility (docs/slides to video) is the differentiator to test.

news.body: Taiwan indicted nine people, including a senior Nvidia manager and two Super Micro employees, over an alleged AI chip smuggling scheme. They're accused of concealing illegal shipments of US-controlled AI servers into China in violation of US export controls; the primary charges are breach of trust and document forgery.
news.means: A reminder that export-control enforcement now reaches individual employees at major vendors, not just corporate compliance -- relevant context if a client sources AI hardware through resellers or distributors.

news.body: Sam Altman says slow agentic AI adoption comes down to 'economic inertia,' not a technology gap. 66% of companies cite security risk as their top AI concern; the companies successfully scaling agents share three traits: single-responsibility agents with narrow scope, mandatory written logs of every agent decision, and human review checkpoints before high-stakes actions.
news.means: A ready-made governance framework for client agent rollouts -- narrow scope, audit logs, and human checkpoints before high-stakes actions is a concrete pitch you can bring to a kickoff this week.
